constraints: Developer-built regular wheel installation checked within the interpreter that imports the selected seven files; Linux/macOS/Windows matrix declares Python 3.9 and 3.13.
Offline comparison of selected import locations, source bytes and installed RECORD metadata. No runtime, native ABI, device or throughput requirement.
alternatives: Python standard-library importlib.metadata inside the tested interpreter.
Node child_process or Java ProcessBuilder driving Python metadata inspection.
rationale: KEEP direct Python metadata inspection because Distribution.files and locate_file connect the selected distribution records to the actual imported paths in the same interpreter. Six methods with real temporary dist-info files check unique membership, location, hash and size.

pip inspect provides an environment report, while uv can inspect installed packages/files. Neither report alone performs this selected source-byte and actual-import association. Using another executable requires proving it selected the same interpreter/environment.

Node and Java can supervise Python processes, but the import-location evidence must still come from the tested Python interpreter. No independent process-orchestration requirement or measured performance constraint justifies another runtime for this check.

The existing byte comparison intentionally accepts identical external copies. The new RECORD check rejects a copy not at the path resolved for its selected distribution entry. Five negative methods produce nine assertion failures when only the new check is replaced with a no-op.
limits: RECORD, metadata and checkout are local trusted-build inputs, not signatures or artifact authentication. Imported package code executes before checking.
Only seven selected files are associated with the distribution returned by the interpreter. No global uniqueness scan, dependency closure, bytecode attestation or whole-wheel authentication.
The distribution version is not compared with project metadata. This slice checks selected member association, not release-version identity.
The SHA-256/size requirement is specific to this regular wheel CI profile; broader installed-project formats may legally omit fields.
Existing Linux Python 3.13 installation reused; no new wheel/build/clean environment or remote matrix success. Files are reread without an atomic snapshot.
